themes_detail.label: Garbage collection collapse
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 6,300% increase (z-score: 23.81)—suggesting a potential sanitation service failure or route disruption in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 8 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (6,300% spike, z-score 23.81)
Aligns with long-standing Community Board budget request for increased sanitation trucks and equipment
Peak of 8 complaints in single week represents unprecedented volume in 90-day complaint history
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if a specific truck or route was out of service this week and what triggered the failure
Interview residents on affected blocks about pickup delays and overflow conditions
Cross-reference with Blocked Driveway complaints (up 122% 2 weeks ago) to map whether garbage trucks couldn't access certain areas

themes_detail.label: Residential trash disposal surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential Disposal Complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK versus a 1.9-complaint weekly average (220% increase, z-score: 5.28), indicating residents are reporting violations or improper handling of building waste.
evidence: 6 Residential Disposal Complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (220% spike, z-score 5.28)
Spike occurred in same week as Missed Collection crisis, suggesting linked waste management breakdown
Pattern suggests building-level disposal issues rather than street-level contamination alone
reporting_angles: Determine whether missed pickups are forcing residents to violate disposal rules or whether building operators are not complying with DSNY procedures
Interview building managers to understand whether they're struggling with cart space, overflow, or frequency of service
Check DOE permit filings for any recent changes to waste handling at institutional buildings (schools, hospitals) in the district

themes_detail.label: Animal waste and dead animal spike
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, Dead Animal complaints spiked to 3 (2,300% above the 0.1 weekly baseline) and Unsanitary Animal Pvt Property complaints reached 5 last week (1,233% increase), suggesting a possible animal infestation, die-off event, or pest control failure linked to sanitation breakdown.
evidence: 3 Dead Animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
5 Unsanitary Animal Pvt Property complaints last week vs. 0.4 baseline (1,233% spike, z-score 9.55)
Spike correlates temporally with garbage collection collapse, suggesting overflowing trash attracting or trapping animals
Animal/pest control is a recurring Community Board budget request, signaling chronic capacity issues at DOHMH
reporting_angles: Investigate whether dead animals are concentrated in specific blocks or building types (residential vs. commercial)
Interview DOHMH or pest control vendors about whether missed trash collection is creating conditions for rodent population surge
Locate residents near reported dead animal complaints to document health/nuisance impacts and gather street-level photography

themes_detail.label: Building exterior maintenance deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Outside Building complaints surged to 6 last week versus a 0.8 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 7.94), suggesting widespread structural, facade, or exterior condition violations in residential or commercial properties.
evidence: 6 Outside Building complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 7.94)
Building/Use complaints also up 392% 3 weeks ago (8 complaints vs. 1.6 baseline), suggesting broader building code violations
377 DOB Alteration filings in last 90 days (with only 10 new buildings) indicates ongoing renovation activity, potentially creating code violations
reporting_angles: Cross-reference Outside Building complaint locations with DOB Alteration filings to see if unpermitted work or incomplete permits are driving violations
Determine whether the spike corresponds to a specific weather event (rain/wind damage) or systemic maintenance failure
Photograph affected buildings and interview residents about safety concerns (falling debris, structural instability)

themes_detail.label: Heat/hot water emergency response surge
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team (ERT) complaints spiked to 3 two weeks ago versus a 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% increase, z-score: 8.69), indicating a cluster of urgent heating system failures or dangerous conditions requiring emergency city response.
evidence: 3 ERT complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Heat/Hot Water dominates 90-day complaint volume (5,116 complaints total), indicating chronic systemic issue in district
ERT spike occurred at onset of winter season when heating demands peak
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings triggered ERT response and whether they have history of violations or deferred maintenance
Interview residents in buildings that required emergency response about how long they went without heat and what temperatures they endured
Cross-check with DOE capital budget requests (recurring) to see if aging building infrastructure is driving failures
